lastReleaseMessage: Seven aged findings closed: Stripe idempotency, a real gate on two release steps, one cron budget, and 31 percent off the icons

milestone.label: v0.16 - Supabase auth + Stripe subscriptions + live TICA data pipeline

items: RE-COUNTED 2026-09-02 against the same eight gates and HELD at 84, because no gate moved. The counting rule is written down here so the next audit can re-derive the number in a minute instead of asking the question a fourth time: each of the eight version-one gates in the Version-one scope section of PROJECT_SPEC.md is worth 12.5 points, a gate scores full when it is shipped, and a gate whose code is finished but whose last step is a ruling or a reading nobody has taken yet scores partial. Six gates are shipped, so the floor is 75. The two open gates, the free-tier measurement and the billing enforcement flag, are both code-complete with one non-code step left each, so the defensible band runs from 75 at no credit to 87.5 at half credit, and 84 sits inside it. What happened since the 2026-08-26 anchor is repair work on gates that were already counted, not a gate closing: v0.18.0 fixed a Stripe webhook that had answered 500 on every delivery since the event log landed, migration 0012 granted back the execute permission migration 0009 revoked, and v0.18.1 made the audit trail say so when its durable write fails. The billing gate is in better shape than it was on the anchor date and still is not enforcing, so the number stays where it is. Moving it needs a gate to close.

RE-COUNTED 2026-08-26 against an approved scope, which is why the number finally moved. It sat at 76 through three reviews because the completion question could not be answered while the freeze-versus-phase-two decision was open: a percentage needs a denominator, and there was not one. Kane ruled keep building, under a no-cost-increase constraint, and the scope is now eight gates written into the Version-one scope section of PROJECT_SPEC.md. Six of the eight are shipped. Three of them closed today in v0.17.36: data stewardship (export, erasure, retention policy, public retention page), durability (the community judge ratings now have a daily Postgres snapshot, migration 0010, and were the last dataset with no second copy), and the code half of running inside the free tier. Four surfaces moved out of the count entirely rather than being finished, and that is a real part of the change: the ten-table relational schema in 0001_init.sql is parked in the file itself, along with ownership certificate verification, the invite flow, and merged co-ownership. They were counting against completion while nobody intended to build them.
Billing gate: the Stripe subscription path is code-complete and one environment flag (SUBSCRIPTION_GATE_ENFORCE) from enforcing. Turning it on or deciding not to is the open gate.

Free-tier measurement: the write budget is now understood and the code is inside it, but nobody has read the actual key-value write counts off the Cloudflare dashboard. That reading needs an account token this session was not permitted to use, so the arithmetic in PROJECT_SPEC.md is unverified against real traffic.
Judge-panel coverage keeps converging by cron. Ongoing by design, not a gate that closes.

Security: view-as and shared-cats still read the key-value store rather than security-definer remote calls, so the two cross-account paths lack the database-enforced boundary that own-data reads have. Carried, not scoped as a version-one gate.

barRaise.topFinding: Both high findings from the previous run closed in code, with tests, and nothing serious opened behind them: a daily reconciliation leg now diffs the live subscription list against stored profiles independent of webhook delivery, and the state-save route carries a per-identity limit plus a degraded answer when its durable write fails. What remains is a long tail of sixty medium items, and that tail is the problem rather than any single row. Twenty-one commits now sit above the shipped version, with the changelog naming seven of them from 2026-09-04.
barRaise.reconcileNote: 2026-09-18 close reconciliation, both legs. Ten findings from the 2026-09-11 run were marked completed in the queue archive and each was re-read against the tree at 562be21 before closing: reliability-23, reliability-24, reliability-25, reliability-20, security-19, data-integrity-27, data-integrity-28, auth-token-hygiene-03, release-ps1-stack-04, compliance-data-steward-04. data-integrity-29 was NOT closed despite its queue row, because migration 0014 is on disk and unapplied, so the deployed prune is still the 0010 body; it moved to the deferred list instead. Five more ids left the counted set by a severity downgrade rather than a fix and are excluded from actionsClosed: reliability-22, performance-03, cost-economics-03, auth-token-hygiene-06, gate-page-publish-03.

closedLog.evidence: an event type this app does not act on is stamped ignored rather than applied, through a new stripe_event_ignore function in migration 0013, so an ignored delivery stops raising the per-customer staleness watermark. Commit 490bb15, with a new webhook test and the migration probe updated to six guarded functions. Commit da90f1b then made the stamp survive a worker deployed ahead of its migration: a

handleUserDelete erases the durable copy first and aborts with 502 postgres_unavailable before touching any key-value store when that erasure is not confirmed, so an outage can no longer destroy the fast copy, the sharing grants and the vote markers while the durable account row survives. Commit 490bb15, with two new tests. Verified 2026-09-04 by running npm test in X:/YesAndRing: 144 of 144 pass.

handleStatePost reads the last written blob and skips both writes when the incoming state and name are unchanged under a stable serialization, reporting unchanged, and PROJECT_SPEC.md gains the write-volume row in the cost table. Commits 490bb15 and dc21e28, with a new four-case test covering the no-op skip, a key-order-only change, a real edit and the first save. Verified 2026-09-04 by running np
REDACTED: this text named a weakness and the file it lives in, which together are an address. Severity and project are kept; the location is in the project's own report under X:\PortfolioOps.

The scheduled handler has one key-value budget, CRON_KV_SHARES, and every leg draws its share from it instead of carrying its own constant; SNAPSHOT_KV_CAP and PURGE_WRITES_PER_RUN are gone and PARITY_KV_CAP reads the table. The shares are reserved before any leg starts rather than drawn as they run, because the legs run concurrently and a race is not an ordering. The legs are reordered so the backup and the erasure debt go first, those being the two that cannot be made up on a later run. Monday is the tight day at 1000 operations exactly, and the cut fell on the parity probe rather than the backup: the snapshot keeps the 400 per prefix it has always walked, and a truncated parity walk already stamps itself truncated and reaches the cron error sink.

The feedback webhook has a row in the handler's webhook table, naming its binding (DISCORD_FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK, a Worker secret rather than a file) and both things it carries. Its channel is stated as not recorded anywhere in the repository, with how to read it, rather than guessed from the category's five names. All three state-parity reports now go through reportParityPost, which checks the delivery the way the drift branch already did and records a failed report in the cron error sink under the name of the report that never landed.

The skip message and both example headers name X:\.secrets\YesAndRing\scripts, which is where discord-notify.ps1 actually reads the webhook files from, and each example says plainly that a copy left in scripts\ is never read. The dev-log example also lost a mis-encoded long dash and a stale reference to the webhook's old default name.

The sixty-three breed icons are reduced from three decimal places to one, which is under a fifteenth of a pixel at the 512-pixel size the app draws them. Measured: 4.30 MB to 3.30 MB on disk, 1.74 MB to 1.20 MB over the wire after compression, a 31 percent cut in what crosses. Rendering checked side by side at 256 and 28 pixels against the kept originals, including the Selkirk Rex, which carries the densest line work of the set, with no visible difference. scripts/reduce-breed-icons.py does the reduction and its --check mode is a release gate, so a newly traced icon at full precision stops a ship rather than landing.

Both steps can now stop a release, so the handler's seven-gate sentence is true. The BUILD stamp reads public/index.html back and aborts if the stamp it just wrote is not in it, because a missed stamp serves a stale shell to every returning visitor. The version bump reads all four rewritten files back and aborts naming the file that did not take, because five files that all silently kept the old version agree with each other perfectly and the later pill check passes.
public/sw.js joined check-version-pill.ps1's comparison set, which now reads five sources rather than four and reports all five. Verified against the live tree: every source reads v0.18.2.

stripeForm takes an idempotency key and sends it as the idempotency-key header, and getOrCreateStripeCustomer derives a stable one from the account identifier, so a checkout that times out after Stripe made the customer retries into the same customer instead of a second one. Three tests in test/stripe-idempotency.test.js pin the header, the no-key case, and that two runs for the same account send the same key. The checkout and portal session calls stay unkeyed on purpose: keying those by account would hand a person the previous session when they asked for a new one.
